fields.title: Goals: how a measurable goal differs from a slogan
fields.keyTakeaway: A good goal names a result, not work, and it cannot be achieved without changing anything in substance. If a goal is completed by releasing a feature, it's a work plan, not a goal.
fields.checkQuestion: "Release social features by June" — why is this not a goal?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key question of the node: **what targets to achieve?** In block G2 we tested hypotheses; here, it's how to set what they are tested for.
fields.blocks/1/text: Running example: Vetka is a fictional subscription book reading app, 400 thousand active monthly users.
fields.blocks/2/subtitle: Five questions; failing any of them means rework
fields.blocks/2/items/0: **Is it a result or work?** "Increase the share of people finishing their first book to 40%" is a result. "Release reminders" is work.
fields.blocks/2/items/1: **Can it be met formally?** If yes — find out how and close that loophole in advance.
fields.blocks/2/items/2: **Is there a number and a deadline?** Without them, a goal cannot be discussed, only retold.
fields.blocks/2/items/3: **Is it realistic?** The benchmark is past dynamics: a goal requiring tenfold growth without changing conditions is demotivating.
fields.blocks/2/items/4: **Who is accountable?** One person, not a department.
fields.blocks/3/text: **OKR adds a useful distinction:** the objective is phrased in words and explains why it matters, while two to four key results use numbers that show whether it was achieved. Key results are not tasks; tasks live separately and can change until the result is achieved.
fields.blocks/4/text:
Before: "Launch social features and increase engagement."

After:
Objective — the reader finishes their first book, because those who finish renew their subscription 2.3 times more often.
Key Result 1 — share of readers finishing their first book up from 31% to 40%.
Key Result 2 — share of readers dropping on chapter two down from 44% to 35%.
Guardrail — notification unsubscribes no higher than 8%.
Owner — reading product manager.

Social features remained on the list of hypotheses that might help with this, or might fail testing.
fields.blocks/4/title: Vetka, how a quarterly goal was rewritten
fields.blocks/5/text: As soon as people are paid for a number, a way is found to boost it without value. Therefore, a guardrail metric is placed next to every goal, specifying that its degradation zeroes out the achievement.
fields.blocks/5/title: A goal tied to a bonus takes on a life of its own
fields.blocks/6/text: Not all work belongs in goals. Support, tech debt, customer commitments exist independently; trying to express them through ambitious numbers turns goals into bureaucracy.
